newsitem.title: USA: Delta forecasts rise as Q2 earnings near.
newsitem.headline: Delta forecasts rise as Q2 earnings near.

text.p: Forecasts for Delta Air Lines Inc's earnings in the second fiscal quarter have risen sharply with the approach of company's reporting date.
As recently as two weeks ago, the Wall Street consensus estimate was $1.21 per share for the No. 3 U.S. carrier, up 30 percent from the year-earlier $0.93, according to First Call.
Now, with the results due Thursday, the First Call consensus has jumped to $1.40 per share, which would represent a whopping 51 percent increase for the quarter, which ended December 31.

"The (Delta) numbers are not bad at all, despite a huge run-up in fuel costs," said analyst Julius Maldutis of Salomon Brothers. "Traffic growth in December was an astonishing 12 percent for the industry, capacity's under relatively good control, and the fundamentals look like we'll have another good year."

On paper, Maldutis has been expecting Delta to earn $1.30 a share for the second quarter. But he said Tuesday that $1.40 sounded like a good figure, considering recent company news and the general health of the industry.
At least eight analysts have raised their estimates on Delta since the company announced last week that second quarter costs would be lower and non-passenger revenues higher than anticipated.
The rising forecasts continue to affect Delta's stock, which was up another 1-3/8 Tuesday afternoon to 81 on the New York Stock Exchange after sizable gains last week.

In addition to lower costs and higher non-passenger revenues, Wall Street's imagination has been captured by reports of success at Delta Express, the new low-cost service launched by the carrier in November.

Delta's December traffic growth, which outstripped the industry's by more than four percentage points, was said to bode well for the venture, which was launched as a retaliatory strike against discounters including ValuJet Inc and Southwest Airlines Co.
"I think that's a great success story," said Maldutis.

But some analysts said the express service was important only alongside other factors, including better-than-expected revenues from code-sharing agreements with foreign carriers, and the marketing of frequent-flier miles.
"Delta Express is only something like three percent of their system capacity," said Susan Donofrio of NatWest Securities Corp.
"It's just one of a number of revenue opportunites that Delta is trying to do. Another one, obviously, is the reshuffling of trans-Atlantic flights.
"As a stand-alone, I don't think (Delta Express) is as important. But cobbled together with a number of initiatives, it is important."
Donofrio expects Delta to report second quarter earnings of $1.35 per share.
